themes_detail.label: Street Light Outages Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints spiked to 25 THIS WEEK, a 147% jump from the 10.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden infrastructure failure affecting neighborhood safety and visibility across Upper West Side.
evidence: 25 street light condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.39)
147% increase represents sudden spike, not gradual deterioration
Likely affects multiple blocks/neighborhoods simultaneously given magnitude
reporting_angles: Investigate whether citywide Con Edison outages or localized infrastructure failure is responsible
Interview residents about safety impacts, especially in evening hours; check whether crime incidents correlate with outages
Request Department of Transportation timeline for repairs; compare response time to other neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Street Damage Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 170 LAST WEEK, a 295% surge from the 43.0 weekly average, representing the largest sustained street infrastructure crisis in the 8-week baseline period and affecting pedestrian safety and vehicle traffic.
evidence: 170 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 43.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.87)
295% increase is largest spike in dataset; suggests concentrated deterioration event
1,145 DOB permit filings in last 90 days with 1,059 alterations indicate ongoing construction/infrastructure work that may be collateral damage source
reporting_angles: Map the 170 complaints geographically—are they concentrated on specific avenues or blocks? Is there a construction project correlation?
Interview DOT about backlog and repair timeline; cross-reference with permit filings to determine if construction is exacerbating pothole problem
Document resident impact: commuters, elderly residents navigating wheelchair-unfriendly terrain, bike accidents

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, a 1100% spike from a 0.5 weekly baseline, indicating a sudden change in park usage patterns or enforcement—a dramatic anomaly that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 6 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.78, severity: high)
1100% increase is statistically extreme; baseline is near-zero, making spike highly visible to residents
Likely concentrated in single park or specific time window given magnitude
reporting_angles: Which park(s) generated the complaints? (Riverside, Central Park border, or smaller neighborhood park?)
What type of noise: music events, street performers, construction, recreational noise? Has NYPD or Parks Dept permitted new events?
Interview Parks Dept about any recent policy changes, event permits, or closure/reopening of facilities

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Cutting
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints reached 5 LAST WEEK, a 344% increase from the 1.1 weekly average, suggesting either coordinated tree removal or a surge in resident reports of previously unreported damage in the district.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.68)
344% increase concentrated in single week; pattern suggests clustered incident rather than ongoing low-level problem
DOB data shows 1,145 active permits; potential correlation with alteration work affecting street trees
reporting_angles: Request Parks Dept data on tree removals filed in past 2 weeks—compare to complaints to identify which are legitimate vs. illegal
Interview residents on which streets/corners saw damage; photo documentation of stumps or cut branches
Investigate whether construction permits correlate with tree damage (developer clearing trees for building work)

themes_detail.label: Animal Neglect Reports Rise
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK, a 433% increase from a 0.8 weekly baseline, indicating either a specific neglect case or emerging animal welfare concerns in residential buildings across the district.
evidence: 4 unsanitary animal private property complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.91)
433% spike is significant but raw numbers are small, suggesting either one building with multiple violations or scattered incidents
Baseline near-zero means even small increase appears statistically extreme
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaints with building addresses—are they from one building or multiple locations?
Contact Department of Health Animal Care and Control for case details; determine if one hoarding situation or multiple neglect cases
If concentrated in one building, investigate landlord/owner compliance history and tenant conditions
